title: Grant <-> work linkage where the work declares the grant and an open registry resolves it

rule.confirmed: the publication's own funding metadata (Europe PMC grantsList, PubMed GrantList, or Crossref funder[].award[]) declares a grant number, AND that number resolves in NIH RePORTER (core_project_num echoed by the registry) or in the CORDIS project index
rule.candidate: declared but not resolvable: the funder has no open registry in this source set, or the CORDIS lookup found nothing
rule.rejected: declared as an NIH-style number but RePORTER holds no project with that core
rule.reverse_direction_blocked: starting from a grant and listing its publications is NOT possible: NIH RePORTER does not carry publication identifiers in the v2 search response, and CORDIS has no publication index (probe cordis_no_publication_index: HTTP 500 'no such index [publication]')

worked_example_of_why_confidence_matters.declared_by: Europe PMC grantsList, PubMed GrantList AND Crossref funder[].award[] - all three agree the paper declares H2020 grant 831644
worked_example_of_why_confidence_matters.why_it_matters: the number match is machine-verified, yet an ageing/ICU paper is improbably funded by the EOSC secretariat project. That is a publication-metadata error, and no amount of identifier matching fixes it. This is why every CONFIRMED here is scoped to 'the number matches', never to 'the grant funded this work'.
